examples.translation: to be wrecked; to have an accident (train, ship, plane, etc.)
examples.english: to be wrecked; to have an accident (train, ship, plane, etc.)

glosses: shipwreck, shipwrecking, sinking (an event in which a ship sinks or runs aground)
действие по значению гл. крушить, крушиться; ломка, физическое уничтожение чего-либо, обычно с особой яростью

examples.text: Предметная агрессия — это агрессия, направленная на окружающие предметы. Проявляется она путем биения посуды, крушения мебели и прочих предметов обихода.

glosses: несчастный случай с транспортным средством; авария, катастрофа в пути

examples.text: Я очень медленно подвигался вперёд, но пароход с низовьев мог прийти не раньше как через две недели, а за это время я мог быть уже на месте крушения и определить, спасена ли какая-нибудь часть груза.
27 ноября 1996 года 23 человека, в том числе двое детей, погибли в результате крушения военно-транспортного самолёта Ил-76 под Абаканом.

glosses: перен. гибель, прекращение существования или полная утрата чего-либо

examples.text: И его собственное жизненное крушение было окутано в его глазах такой чёрной безнадёжностью оттого, что он сознавал его как эпизод крушения всего своего класса.

translations.source_sense_description: несчастный случай с транспортным средством; авария, катастрофа в пути

glosses: Something or someone that has been ruined.

examples.text: He was an emotional wreck after the death of his wife.

glosses: The remains of something that has been severely damaged or worn down.

examples.text: To the fair haven of my native home, / The vvreck of vvhat I was, fatigued I come, […]

glosses: An event in which something is damaged through collision.

examples.text: Hard and obſtinate, / As is a rocke amidſt the raging floods: / gaynſt vvhich a ſhip of ſuccour deſolate, / doth ſuffer vvreck both of her ſelfe and goods.
the wrecks of matter and the crush of worlds
Its intellectual life was thus able to go on amidst the wreck of its political life.

glosses: An event in which something is damaged through collision.
A shipwreck: an event in which a ship is heavily damaged or destroyed.
Goods, etc. cast ashore by the sea after a shipwreck.

examples.text: 2. ... Wreck includes the cargo, stores and tackle of a vessel and all parts of a vessel separated from the vessel, and the property of persons who belong to, are on board or have quitted a vessel that is wrecked, stranded or in distress at any place in Canada.

glosses: A large number of birds that have been brought to the ground, injured or dead, by extremely adverse weather.

examples.text: [I]n 1952 more than 7,000 were involved in such a "wreck" in Britain and Ireland.

glosses: To destroy violently; to cause severe damage to something, to a point where it no longer works, or is useless.

examples.text: He wrecked the car in a collision.
That adulterous hussy wrecked my marriage!
Supposing that they saw the king's ship wrecked.

glosses: To ruin or dilapidate.
To plunder goods from wrecked ships.
To dismantle wrecked vehicles or other objects, to reclaim any useful parts.
To involve in a wreck; hence, to cause to suffer ruin; to balk of success, and bring disaster on.

examples.text: Weak and envy'd, if they should conspire, / They wreck themselves, and he hath his Desire.

glosses: To be involved in a wreck; to be damaged or destroyed.

examples.text: […] Mrs. Marleen Ketchum was not quite certain if the train wrecked or if the volcano blew its top. It took a moment before she was certain it had to be the passenger train.

translations.source_sense_description: несчастный случай с транспортным средством; авария, катастрофа в пути

glosses: The remains of a destroyed or dilapidated construction, such as a house or castle.

examples.text: The Veian and the Gabian towirs shall fall, / And one promiscuous ruin cover all; / Nor, after length of years, a stone betray / The place where once the very ruins lay.
The labour of a day will not build up a virtuous habit on the ruins of an old and vicious character.

A canister of flour from the kitchen had been thrown at the looking-glass and lay like trampled snow over the remains of a decent blue suit with the lining ripped out which lay on top of the ruin of a plastic wardrobe.
Dr. Manuel: No one is saved. The age of humanity is ended. Soon, only ruin and corpses will remain.
Not only is Jerusalem not a ruin, but she is at the height of her glory compared to all of Jewish history!

glosses: The state of being a ruin, destroyed or decayed.

examples.text: The monastery has fallen into ruin.

glosses: Something that leads to serious trouble or destruction.

examples.text: Gambling has been the ruin of many.
The errors of young men are the ruin of business.

The Bat—they called him the Bat.[…]. He[…]played a lone hand,[…]. Most lone wolves had a moll at any rate—women were their ruin—but if the Bat had a moll, not even the grapevine telegraph could locate her.

glosses: The act of ruining something.
A fall or tumble.

examples.text: His ruin startled th’ other steeds.

glosses: A change that destroys or defeats something; destruction; overthrow.

examples.text: the ruin of a ship or an army
the ruin of a constitution or a government
the ruin of health or hopes

Oh Portius, is there not some choſen Curſe,
Some hidden Thunder in the Stores of Heav’n,
Red with uncommon Wrath, to blaſt the Man
Who owes his Greatneſs to his Country’s Ruin?
Ruin seize thee, ruthless king!

glosses: Complete financial loss; bankruptcy.
To cause the fiscal ruin of; to bankrupt or drive out of business.

examples.text: With all these purchases, you surely mean to ruin us!
In one way, indeed, he bade fair to ruin us; for he kept on staying week after week, and at last month after month, so that all the money had been long exhausted...

glosses: To destroy or render something no longer usable or operable.

examples.text: He ruined his new white slacks by accidentally spilling oil on them.
By the fireside there are old men seated, / Seeing ruined cities in the ashes.

glosses: To upset or overturn the plans or progress of, or to have a disastrous effect on something.

examples.text: My car breaking down just as I was on the road ruined my vacation.

glosses: To make something less enjoyable or likeable.

examples.text: I used to love that song, but being assaulted when that song was playing ruined the song for me.

glosses: To reveal the ending of (a story); to spoil.
To fall into a state of decay.

examples.text: Though he his house of polisht marble build, / Yet shall it ruine like the Moth's fraile cell

glosses: To seduce or debauch, and thus harm the social standing of.

examples.text: The young libertine was notorious for ruining local girls.

translations.source_sense_description: гибель, прекращение существования или полная утрата чего-либо

glosses: A precipitous decline in fortune; death or rapid deterioration, as in status or wealth.

examples.text: Many economic and political reasons led to the downfall of the Roman Empire.

The Black Cats contributed to their own downfall for the only goal when Titus Bramble, making his first appearance since Boxing Day, and Michael Turner, let Phil Jones' cross bounce across the six-yard box as [Wayne] Rooney tucked in at the back post.

glosses: The cause of such a fall; a critical blow or error.

examples.text:
Orson Scott Card
It is the downfall of evil, that it never sees far enough ahead.

glosses: An act of falling down.

examples.text: a downfall of rain

[T]he prominent character of leading young lady or heroine, which Paula was to personate, was really the most satisfactory in the whole list for her. For although she was to be wooed hard, there was just as much love-making among the remaining personages; while, as Somerset had understood the play, there could occur no flingings of her person upon her lover's neck, or agonized downfalls upon the stage, in her whole performance, [...]

glosses: To fall down; deteriorate; decline.

examples.text: [...] wants to make civilization his subject, he will have a hard time proceeding with the sentence unless collapse is in his active vocabulary, for he cannot say "our civilization will downfall" or "fall down."
Common belief has been that in the future the number of middle managers will downfall due to empowerment and team-building.
It should be noted that the magnitude of satellites decreases when tuning out of degeneracy, and in the wavelength range of 1.2-1.3 pm it downfalls to the value of 10-15% of the main spike magnitude.
[...] As goodly air as ever From lunar orb downfell— Be it by hazard, Or supervened it by arrogancy?

translations.source_sense_description: гибель, прекращение существования или полная утрата чего-либо

glosses: To break apart and fall down suddenly; to cave in.

examples.text: A balloon collapses when the gas escapes from it.

glosses: To cease to function due to a sudden breakdown; to fail suddenly and completely.

examples.text: Pyramid schemes tend to generate profits for a while and then collapse.
However much we like to think of ourselves as something special in world history, in fact industrial societies are subject to the same principles that caused earlier societies to collapse.

glosses: To fold compactly.
In a hierarchical list (such as a directory tree or table of contents), to hide the subentries of (an entry).
To suffer a batting collapse.

examples.text: Immediately after his wicket the team collapsed for 69.

glosses: To cause something to collapse.

examples.text: Hurry up and collapse the tent so we can get moving.
Thomas added: "We presented our experiences of frantically trying to collapse a pram, surrounded by loads of grumpy commuters.

glosses: To pass out and fall to the floor or ground, as from exhaustion or other illness; to faint.

examples.text: The exhausted singer collapsed on stage and had to be taken to the hospital.

glosses: The act of collapsing.

examples.text: She suffered a terrible collapse after slipping on the wet floor.
The top six are assured of continental competition and after making a statement of intent against Stoke, it would take a dramatic collapse for Newcastle to surrender their place.
However the collapse in demand for rail and air travel caused by the pandemic has had a knock-on effect for the project's funding.

glosses: Constant function, one-valued function (in automata theory) (in particular application causing a reset).
Ellipsis of batting collapse.
